newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures continue weak with cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures continue weak with cash.

text.p: CME lumber futures were pressured by the slow and generally weak cash lumber market in early dealings, traders said.

Continued overall slow cash trade weighed further on futures and July moved down to a new low for the move before recovering slightly. Liquidation continued in May as it became the spot month and now has no trading limits, traders said.
Cash sources said that although mills are asking $395 to $400 per tbf for their wood, most trading has taken place in the $382 to $386 area. Wholesalers continue to discount lumber, they said.
At 0931 CDT, lumber posted losses of $4.10 to $3.40 with May off most at $399.00 and July off $3.30 at $392.00 per tbf.
